title: Salvaggio's Lombardo-style band
summary: Coquille's first job was with Joseph Salvaggio's Lombardo-type kid band; they rehearsed hard, played West End roof jobs, and he left after about three years for the Blue Parody hoping to reach the Streeman band.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Except it came out in English. So your very first job was with Joseph Salvaggio, and you say it was something like Lombardo style.
It was a Lombardo type band, Dick.
Did he ever have a mellophone?

No, but we had a boy that played the bass horn, like Lombardo has. And after four hour rehearsals two or three times a week, one year later, it really sounded great. We really, then we began getting jobs on a West End roof, and spot jobs. We all had things to do in a day, so we couldn't take steady work. We were a bunch of kids. And it really sounded good. It's just that after three years, I was ready to make a move to play a different type of music. With all due respect to the Lombardo type of music, I loved it, but I wanted to play something with more of a lift, you know. That's why I moved to the Blue Parody in the hopes of someday getting with Al Streaming.
